hints.title: Complete Tree Level-Order Invariance
hints.text: In a complete binary tree, all levels except possibly the last are full, and all nodes in the last level are as far left as possible.

hints.title: BFS Null Encounter Property
hints.text: During a level-order traversal, once a null node is encountered, no subsequent non-null node can ever appear.

hints.title: Queue Traversal with Null Sentinel
hints.text: Enqueue root into a queue. While queue is not empty, pop the front node. If node is None, set seen_none = True. If node is not None and seen_none is True, return False. Otherwise enqueue its left and right children. Return True.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of nodes in binary tree
W: maximum tree width (up to N/2)
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking parent pointer child existence recursively without BFS level tracking easily misses gaps in intermediate levels.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Level-order queue traversal visits each node and null pointer exactly once, using queue space proportional to tree width.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that a complete binary tree allows no non-null node to follow any null in level-order traversal.
complexity.notes: Standard level-order traversal with enqueued null pointers makes the gap detection trivial.
